solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Tanner wastes Palm Sunday taking 24 hours off

indicators.note: to waste something is to ruin it, so the letters of the festival's name are mangled into a new order

parts.note: a day is a period of twenty-four hours, and these letters are taken off before the rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone squanders the Sunday before Easter by skipping a whole day of it.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the letters of PALM SUNDAY, with DAY ('24 hours') taken off, leave PALMSUN, which 'wastes' scrambles into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A device giving ultraviolet light is used to brown the skin, so it is something that tans.

clue.text: At home in safe job requiring little work

indicators.note: in tells us the first piece goes inside the second

parts.note: secure means safe
to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: Working from home in a secure position that asks very little.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'At home' is the inserted piece and the second 'in' is the container signal, so the clue word 'in' does two different-looking jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: A post that pays but demands almost no effort is a cushy office, originally a church benefice without duties.

clue.text: Material for grannie with damaged knee

parts.note: nan is an informal word for a grandmother

indicators.note: a damaged knee is put out of shape, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fabric is wanted for an elderly woman who has hurt her leg joint.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a yellowish cotton cloth, originally from Nanjing in China, a kind of fabric.

clue.text: Deathly pale, he sweats — heat is a problem

indicators.note: a problem suggests things are in a mess, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man looks ghastly while perspiring, because the warmth is troubling him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'problem' rearranges HE SWEATS plus HEAT IS A, fifteen letters in all.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom compares a bloodless face to the colour of bed linen, meaning very pale from fear or illness.

clue.text: On which kids go cheaply, flying with two adults

definitions.text: On which kids go cheaply, flying with two adults

indicators.note: flying suggests the letters taking off and landing in a new order

parts.note: A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult, so two of them give AA

explanation.surface: A travel brochure's family offer: children travel at a discount alongside two grown-ups.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer while 'flying' rearranges KIDS GO CHEAPLY plus AA.
explanation.definitionFit: Tour operators sell bundled trips of flight and accommodation, often with child discounts when travelling with parents.

clue.text: Head off plans adopting new standards

indicators.note: to adopt is to take in, so the shortened word takes the new letter inside it
taking the head off means the first letter of the synonym is removed

parts.note: designs are plans or schemes

explanation.surface: Someone is told to forestall schemes by bringing in fresh rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head off' looks like a verb meaning 'prevent'; here it beheads DESIGNS to ESIGNS, and 'adopting' puts N inside after the E.
explanation.definitionFit: Flags carried by regiments or ships are called standards, and these are naval flags.

clue.text: Geezer once sober, drunk with Christmas spirit?

indicators.note: drunk suggests someone unsteady, so the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: An old man who used to be teetotal is now tipsy on festive cheer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges GEEZER ONCE SOBER; geezer is British slang for a man. The question mark flags that the character is a figure of Christmas rather than its cheerful mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's miser in A Christmas Carol is the story's central figure, embodying meanness reformed by festive ghosts.

clue.text: Hanging phrase, it seems — or one that's cancelled

parts.note: to suspend is to hang something up
a sentence is a phrase or group of words

explanation.surface: A grammar point about a dangling phrase, or else one that has been deleted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it seems' marks the playful literal reading, a hanging phrase, built from two synonyms; the definition is the legal sense, a penalty held off.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge may defer a punishment so it is not served unless the offender reoffends, in effect setting it aside.

clue.text: Sticky mixture that's costly for a musician's ability

parts.note: goo is a sticky, gooey substance
dear means expensive or costly

explanation.surface: An expensive sticky concoction is supposed to improve a player's talent.
explanation.definitionFit: Being able to hear pitch accurately is a valued gift for anyone playing music.

clue.text: Cook seen at assembly

indicators.note: to cook the books is to falsify them, so cooking here means rearranging the letters

explanation.surface: A chef was spotted at a gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' looks like a noun, a chef; it is the anagram signal for SEEN AT.
explanation.definitionFit: A legislative chamber, such as the upper house of the US Congress, is a governing assembly.

clue.text: Windies won — Kent gets caught out, when the last man is batting

definitions.text: when the last man is batting

indicators.note: out signals that the letters are put out of their order, rearranged

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A cricket report: the West Indies beat Kent, who are dismissed.
explanation.walkthrough: Windies is a nickname for the West Indies cricket team and Kent is an English county side. 'out' rearranges WINDIESWONKENT plus C. With ten wickets to fall in an innings, the eleventh batsman comes in after the ninth has fallen.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, the final batter of the side walks out once nine of the ten available dismissals have happened.

clue.text: He or Al would appear in full as such

definitions.text: He or Al would appear in full as such

parts.words: He or Al would appear in full as such
parts.note: He and Al read like a man's pronoun and a short name, but they are the symbols for helium and aluminium; written out in full each is the name of one of these substances

explanation.surface: Someone named Al, or some man, would be listed by his full formal title.
explanation.definitionFit: Helium and aluminium are basic substances of the periodic table, each abbreviated to a symbol.

clue.text: Grenade exploded by fireside frames in 1937 B-movie

indicators.note: an exploded grenade is blown to pieces, so its letters are scattered and rearranged

parts.note: fenders are low metal frames set around a fireplace

explanation.surface: A grenade goes off and blows apart the guards around a hearth.
explanation.definitionFit: Range Defenders is a 1937 Republic Pictures western starring the Three Mesquiteers, a low-budget second feature.

clue.text: Supporters shortened epic in capital

parts.note: bras are undergarments that support

indicators.note: shortened means the poem's name loses its final letter

parts.note: the Iliad is Homer's epic poem

explanation.surface: Backers have trimmed a long saga set in a major city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortened' cuts ILIAD to ILIA. The spelling is the Portuguese one.
explanation.definitionFit: This planned city became the seat of Brazil's government in 1960.

clue.text: PM gains much with US vice- president. Right!

parts.note: to win is to gain or obtain
tons, informally, means a lot or much
Mike Pence was vice-president of the United States from 2017 to 2021

explanation.surface: A prime minister benefits greatly alongside an American deputy, and someone exclaims approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right!' reads as an interjection, but it is only R.
explanation.definitionFit: Churchill's full surname was Spencer-Churchill, and he served twice as Britain's Prime Minister.

clue.text: Needing help, Hanoi turns to the French

indicators.note: turns suggests changing shape, so the city's letters are reordered

parts.note: le is the French masculine word for the

explanation.surface: Vietnam's capital, in difficulty, appeals to France for assistance.
explanation.definitionFit: To be stuck in trouble is the idiom, meaning in a difficult situation that needs rescue.

clue.text: Chillax and speak fondly with boorish fellow

parts.note: to coo is to murmur affectionately
a lout is a rough, uncouth man

explanation.surface: Someone is told to relax and murmur sweet nothings with a yob.
explanation.definitionFit: Chillax is slang blending chill and relax; the phrasal verb means calm down.

clue.text: Lack of movement with thoroughfare in its present condition

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a thoroughfare
as is means as it currently stands, without changes

explanation.surface: A road left exactly as it stands shows no motion.
explanation.definitionFit: A state of equilibrium or stagnation is a standstill, where nothing changes.

clue.text: Giant rainstorms ruined such movements

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked, so the letters of the two words are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: Enormous storms disrupted migrations or passages of some kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' scrambles all fifteen letters of GIANT RAINSTORMS; 'such' links the definition to the destroyed storms of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Passing from one place or body to another, as souls are said to do after death, are movements of this kind.

clue.text: Good! Arsenal won with Chelsea first sadly having put the ball in their net!

definitions.text: having put the ball in their net

indicators.note: sadly suggests things going wrong, so the letters are jumbled into a new order
first means only the opening letter of the club's name is used

explanation.surface: A football fan cheers an Arsenal win, then rues a team conceding at their own end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' rearranges GOOD, ARSENAL, WON and C, the first letter of Chelsea. Arsenal and Chelsea are London football clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting the ball into your own side's goal by accident gives the opponents a goal.

clue.text: Busiest assistants catch restful moments

indicators.note: to catch is to hold, so the two words contain the answer within their run of letters

explanation.surface: The hardest-working helpers manage to snatch some rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Short afternoon naps, a custom in hot countries, are times of rest.

clue.text: In real trouble, shock treatment for sort of complex

indicators.note: In places the treatment's letters within the rearranged word
in trouble suggests disorder, so the letters of real are thrown into a new arrangement

parts.note: ECT is electroconvulsive therapy, a treatment using electric shocks

explanation.surface: Someone in serious difficulty receives electric therapy for a psychological condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shock treatment' is the standard crossword clue for ECT, electroconvulsive therapy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Electra complex is a Jungian term for a daughter's attachment to her father.
